exact_version: Sahotra Sarkar and John Stachel, Philosophy of Science 66(2) (June 1999), 208–220; DOI 10.1086/392684. BU CPHS-hosted scan carries the original journal pagination/copyright.
locator: Abstract; Section 2, 'Malament's Result'; Section 3, especially Theorems 1–2, pp. 211–218.
quote: Dropping that assumption, we prove an alternative result
read_scope: Primary PDF body visually read: abstract, Sections 2–3 and Theorems 1–2; checked the argument's setup and theorem conditions. No independent proof reproduction.
findings: The record's central summary is supported. The authors identify invariance under temporal reflections as a premise in Malament's automorphism group; dropping that premise admits forward/backward half-null-cone relations. Their Theorem 1 says Einstein simultaneity is unique when the relation is independent of which parallel observer worldline in an inertial frame is chosen. Theorem 2 makes the backward/forward half-cone relation unique under event-local boost independence plus the condition that no event is simultaneous with another event in its causal future/past. To make the assumptions field auditable, state these distinct conditions rather than the generic 'stated invariance/relational conditions.' The article is a critique and does not replace the primary Malament paper.
downgrade_proposal: None. Keep at full-text with the more exact theorem conditions above; do not treat the critique alone as settling the physical status of temporal-reflection invariance.

exact_version: Allen I. Janis, 'Conventionality of Simultaneity,' Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, archived Winter 2001 edition; page reports first published 1998 and content last modified 1999-06-30.
quote: then S is the relation of standard synchrony
read_scope: Archived SEP secondary entry read through the Malament theorem and its discussion of Sarkar–Stachel; no primary proof verification from this entry.
findings: The frozen record accurately reports the archived SEP summary: the relation is definable from symmetric causal connectibility and inertial observer worldline O, is an equivalence relation, relates at least one point on O to a point off O, and is non-universal; then standard synchrony follows. The SEP itself notes that Malament's result uses time-symmetric causal connectibility and summarizes Sarkar–Stachel's forward/backward null-cone alternatives after temporal-reflection invariance is dropped. This is a verified secondary record, not evidence that the primary Malament theorem had been read.
downgrade_proposal: None for this SEP record; preserve secondary status. It must not stand in for the primary Malament theorem in RC-2.

exact_version: Howard Stein, Philosophy of Science 58(2) (June 1991), 147–167; DOI 10.1086/289609. Cambridge Core confirms title, author, issue/pages, DOI, and abstract; full text read from a Paperzz-hosted scan reproducing the journal pagination.
locator: pp. 148–150, especially the surrounding argument and theorem on p. 150; discussion of physical/interpretive adequacy in Sections II–VI, including p. 159; conclusion pp. 166–167.
quote: Rxy holds if and only if xy is a past-pointing vector
read_scope: Primary article body read from the accessible scan at the theorem and argument level; official Cambridge Core record checked for metadata and abstract. The displayed theorem and surrounding pp. 148–150 argument were read in sequence. No printed-page image comparison, formal proof audit, or independent proof reconstruction.
findings: The sampling-frame record's modest conclusion is supported: Stein argues that special relativity does not rule out event-relative becoming/open-future accounts, and he does not establish physical indeterminism or objective passage. Separate three levels: (1) The accessible OCR's displayed p. 150 THEOREM literally lists reflexivity, transitivity, invariance under time-orientation-preserving automorphisms, and one past-pointing causal related pair, then gives the causal-past biconditional. Taken alone, that statement is false: universal R meets those premises, and reflexive chronological past meets them while omitting past-null pairs. (2) In the immediately preceding pp. 148–150 argument, Stein separately stipulates the causal-influence premise that every point of a's causal past is R-related to a, and earlier condition (iv) requires that at each a some states remain unsettled (hence R is not universal). The argument uses these contextual premises with invariance and transitivity to rule out any extra spacelike/future pair; this is the source-context reading, but comparison against the printed theorem page image was unavailable, so whether the mismatch is print, OCR, or theorem/context extraction remains unresolved. (3) RC-2's project reconstruction—reflexive/transitive/invariant R, full causal-past inclusion, and unsettled condition implying R equals causal past, with premise-necessity countermodels—is a theorem-shaped project objective, not a characterization independently proved by this source spot-check. Case 1 in correspondence-cases.jsonl refutes the four-premise OCR sentence; case 2 refutes adding nonuniversality alone when only one past timelike pair is assumed. Preserve the distinction between the source's event-relative philosophical argument and the project's unproved formal reconstruction.
downgrade_proposal: Keep the source-record's bounded compatibility conclusion, but make its assumptions field explicitly include the all-causal-past inclusion and unsettled condition (iv), and note that these occur in the surrounding argument, not the four-premise displayed OCR sentence. Do not cite the isolated four-premise sentence as a valid characterization. Treat RC-2's context-preserving characterization and necessity table as open project proof obligations; the contextual reconstruction here is not an independent proof verification.

exact_version: Christopher J. Fewster and Rainer Verch, arXiv:1109.6732v2 (8 May 2012); Annales Henri Poincaré 13(7) (2012), 1675–1709; DOI 10.1007/s00023-012-0166-z.
locator: Section 4, 'The massless current'; Theorem 4.3 and adjacent discussion, especially lines 356–422 in the versioned arXiv HTML; Abstract.
quote: dynamically local in LCT₀ for all dimensions n ≥ 2
read_scope: Versioned primary arXiv HTML read at the abstract, model definition, Theorem 4.3 and surrounding construction/counterexample; no independent proof reproduction.
findings: The record's dimension/category claim matches Theorem 4.3. The theorem concerns the massless-current theory J, built from massless scalar solutions modulo locally constant functions, not the unmodified massless Klein–Gordon scalar theory. J is dynamically local for connected-spacetime category Loc₀ in n≥2; for Loc, which permits disconnected spacetimes, it is dynamically local for n≥3 but fails at n=2. The paper gives a disconnected 2D example and calls topological charge a possible remedy a conjecture. Record assumptions and limitations correctly restrict the claim to this model and these categories.
downgrade_proposal: None. Keep the distinction between the massless current quotient and unmodified massless Klein–Gordon theory, and keep the topological-charge remedy labeled as the authors' conjecture.

locator: The sampled locator cites Sections 2–4 and 8–10. The specific matter-entropy decrease/radiation compensation claim is in Section 7, 'Entropy increase from gravitation and nuclear fusion,' especially lines 208–211; broad position summarized in Abstract and Section 10 conclusion.
quote: the entropy decrease in the entropy of matter is more than compensated for by the entropy increase
read_scope: Primary versioned arXiv HTML read at the abstract, Section 7 central discussion, and Section 10 conclusion; bounded claim correspondence only, no independent thermodynamic calculation.
findings: The substantive conclusion is supported within Wallace's bounded statistical-mechanical argument: in the stellar/cosmological discussion, material entropy can decrease while emitted high-entropy radiation compensates; he argues gravity's dynamical role should be distinguished from entropy assigned to gravitational degrees of freedom. The frame's locator omits Section 7, where the recorded specific claim is stated and developed. The claim remains an author's argument, not a general entropy formula or resolution of the Past Hypothesis.
downgrade_proposal: Correct the locator to include Section 7 and retain Section 10 for the summary. No depth downgrade needed for the bounded statement-level spot-check; broader calculations remain unreproduced.

exact_version: David B. Malament, 'Causal Theories of Time and the Conventionality of Simultaneity,' Noûs 11(3) (September 1977), 293–300; DOI 10.2307/2214766. The accessed university-hosted copy is a JSTOR scan of the published article.
locator: Sections 1–3, especially Proposition 1 (p. 296), Proposition 2 and proof sketch (pp. 297–299), and Proposition 3 (p. 299).
quote: Simo is the only relation which satisfies these conditions
read_scope: Primary published article read from the scan at the statement/argument level, including definitions, propositions, proof sketches, and conclusion. No independent proof verification or formalization.
findings: This full-text read resolves the earlier abstract-only status. Malament assumes Minkowski spacetime R⁴ with symmetric causal connectibility K and an inertial observer worldline O. Proposition 2 states that a two-place relation S implicitly definable from K and O, an equivalence relation, and nontrivial by relating a point on O to a point off O must be either standard simultaneity or universal; excluding the universal relation yields standard simultaneity. Proposition 1 gives explicit first-order definability of standard simultaneity. Proposition 3 says a nontrivial equivalence relation implicitly definable from K alone is universal, so no nontrivial absolute simultaneity is recovered. The paper itself presents non-conventionality as conditional on the causal theory of time and its chosen criteria; this is not an unconditional physical or ontological result. The SEP premise summary is substantially accurate but the primary text sharpens the distinction between explicit definability and the weaker automorphism-invariance criterion used in Proposition 2.
downgrade_proposal: None. Propose upgrading the source-register read_depth from abstract to full-text after coordinator integration, with this locator and the conditional status above. Do not call this a proof audit or claim that conventionalism is refuted without the causal-theory bridge premise.
